info.title: sLaunch
info.author: etonedemid
info.details: sLaunch is a fast text based HOME menu replacement inspired by niagara launcher.

changelog:
v0.9.1
sLaunch v0.9.1

Speed, mostly. The menu opens far quicker, Flow scrolls smoothly, and the shelf
can show box art.

 The menu opens much faster

Pressing HOME used to sit on a black screen for a couple of seconds. Almost all
of that was the very first frame: every layout decodes a JPEG for each entry it
is about to draw, so nothing appeared until an image had been decoded for every
icon on screen.

Image loading is now budgeted per frame. The menu draws immediately and the art
fills in over the next handful of frames, which reads as instant.

 Flow scrolls smoothly

Two things were fighting the frame rate.

- Covers were only decoded for a box at the moment it came into view, so a fast
  scroll meant decoding on the frame each new box appeared. Covers are now
  loaded ahead of the row, a few per frame, across a wide margin either side of
  what is on screen.
- Loading was happening in the middle of drawing. Downscaling an image switches
  the render target, which interrupts the frame being drawn; doing that between
  boxes several times a frame is what made scrolling crawl. Everything a frame
  needs is now loaded before any of it is drawn.

Turning a box over is also smooth: the images for the back of a case are large,
and they now load once you have stopped on a game rather than as the selection
sweeps past during a scroll.

The remaining stutter after the menu appeared, and the second of lag coming back
from a game, had the same cause: downscaling an image was done on the GPU by
switching the render target, which flushes the frame being drawn. Every image
load happened while the menu was drawing, so each one tore the frame in half.
Scaling now happens on the CPU and the renderer is only touched to upload the
result.

 Flow: the running game turns

Whichever game is currently running slowly rotates on the shelf, so you can pick
it out of the row at a glance.

 Shelf: vertical covers

Theming > Vertical covers switches the shelf from square tiles to portrait ones,
using the box art Flow has already fetched. Games without a cover fall back to
their icon, centred rather than stretched.

 Also

- Wallpaper blur is computed at a quarter of the size and scaled back up. It is
  a blurred image, so nothing visible is lost, and it is around sixty times less
  work.
- Flow keeps a much larger margin of covers in memory now that there is budget
  for it, so scrolling back and forth does not reload them.
- Start-up is timestamped in slaunch/boot.log if you ever need to see where
  the time goes.

v0.8.0
The cross-media bar comes to sLaunch. New XMB mode (Theming > UI mode) does the PSP thing properly: categories ride a bar across the screen, your games hang below the selected one, and the whole thing is touch-driven - tap a category to open it, drag the column to flick through, tap an entry twice to launch.

Two long-standing annoyances are gone. Closing a homebrew now brings you back to the menu instead of relaunching the homebrew forever, and Restart / Power off now actually restart and power off instead of leaving the console in a weird half-asleep state.

Icon packs are in: drop PNG sets into slaunch/icon_packs// and switch between them in Theming > Icon pack. A clean Minimal pack by @meepcat55 ships in the box. Themes also gained an icon background colour, so packs sit right on any look.

sLaunch now speaks Russian, Japanese, German, Spanish and Chinese - it follows your console's language automatically, and slaunch/lang/template.txt is there if you want to add yours. Korean and Chinese consoles get their proper system font too, and a full Noto Sans CJK is bundled under Theming > Fonts.

Also: dragging anywhere now moves the content under your finger (not the cursor), taps in submenus land where you actually tap, and the welcome screen slimmed down to a quiet two lines that fade in and out.

Install:- run sInstaller.nro, or extract slaunch-v0.8.0-sd.zip to your SD root. Reboot after.

v0.7.0
sLaunch now says hello. On boot (and right after setup) you get a welcome screen that greets you by your Switch profile name over the opening jingle, with a different line each time. Don't want it? Theming > Welcome screen.

You can also clean up the menu now - every system entry (Album, Browser, Settings, Power, Homebrew...) can be shown or hidden in Theming > Menu entries. Theming itself stays put so you can always get back.

New Random game entry: it rolls through your library like a slot machine, lands on something, and launches it.

Setup got restyled to match the rest of the menu instead of looking like its own thing.
